subject: Recap + next steps: Medisync data handling exceptions
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@medisync.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + next steps: Medisync data handling exceptions

Hi Elena — thanks again for the sync earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can move the deal forward.

Call summary (30 min):
- Medisync goal: onboard Redwood for clinical transcription + downstream insights while ensuring PHI never persists beyond short-lived diagnostic windows.
- Main asks: 0-retention for patient-identifiable content in logs & transcripts; clarity on embeddings persistence used for personalization; US data residency and SOC2 evidence for logging/audit.
- Constraints: you need language in contract and a technical deployment option that guarantees no persistent KV or debug logs containing PHI.

Proposed options (high level):
1) Ephemeral mode (recommended): runtime flag that disables persistent write-through caching and drops debug logs with PII, with 0-retention for raw transcripts.
2) Partial carveout: 0-retention for raw transcripts + 7-day TTL for derived artifacts (embeddings) used for personalization — UUIDs only, encrypted at rest, separate key per tenant.
3) Private/Dedicated deployment: VPC + customer KMS and network isolation for full control (required if legal won’t accept shared hosted option).

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Jon as AE: confirm which of the above options aligns with procurement appetite (Elena).
- Ben as SE: provide a short tech note showing how ephemeral_mode works and what evidence we can produce (logs, KV purge).
- Marissa as compliance: draft exception language we can add to the SOW and data processing appendix.

Attachments: I’ve attached a 1-page summary of the options and a draft clause we can iterate on.

Asks for this week: please confirm by EOD Friday if Medisync needs absolute 0-retention across ALL derived artifacts (including embeddings) or if a short TTL (1–14 days) is acceptable for embeddings used for personalization. If you prefer private deployment, let us know and we’ll get architecture and pricing.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up call if that helps.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0196

Attachments: medisync-privacy-ask-summary.pdf, proposed-data-exception-clause.docx

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@medisync.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Alan Cho <alan@medisync.ai>, Medisync Legal <legal@medisync.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Medisync data handling exceptions

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. Couple quick clarifications from our legal and engineering side: 

1) Scope of 0-retention ask: clinical transcripts and any prompt history that contain PHI must be non-persistent in our environment. We can tolerate short-lived artifacts for aggregated analytics only if they contain no linkable identifiers.
2) Embeddings: our clinical team is split. For immediate MVP we can avoid personalization and therefore avoid embedding retention. For longer-term product (risk stratification) we may consider embeddings but only with a TTL <= 7 days and with customer-side encryption keys.
3) Evidence: can Redwood provide a short artifact demonstrating KV purge and a sample audit log showing deletion timestamps? Legal also asked for SOC2 section that details log retention and access controls.

We’re open to private/dedicated if the hosted route can’t meet the 0-retention requirement for PHI in production. Can Ben share a one-pager on ephemeral_mode and what remains in memory vs persisted to disk?

If you can send proposed clause language for our counsel to review, that would speed things up. Alan (CC) will coordinate legal review.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product | Medisync AI
elena@medisync.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Medisync data handling exceptions (technical notes)

Jonas / Marissa — quick technical notes to feed into the clause and customer response. High-level feasibility checks: 

- Ephemeral_mode: implemented in runtime. When ephemeral_mode=true for a tenant, runtime will:
  * disable write-through to long-term logs (no debug.log writes),
  * zero out KV cache on session end and emit a purge event with timestamp,
  * avoid persisting intermediate prompt history to disk; short-lived in-memory ring buffer only.
- KV vs embeddings: the KV cache that stores decoder KV is not the same as derived embeddings store. We can configure embeddings store with a configurable TTL; TTL=0 is supported (transient in-memory only) but will reduce personalization features.
- Audit evidence: we can generate an export showing purge events and a small sample of system audit logs (timestamps, user/tenant id, action) — note this is sanitized before sharing. SOC2: we can reference the control for log retention and provide the report excerpt under NDA.

Open questions / risks to call out: 
- If Medisync wants absolute legal guarantee against any persistent artifact containing PHI in our hosted shared environment, legal may require a dedicated deployment + customer-controlled KMS.
- Embedding TTL=0 eliminates many personalization use-cases (model memory). If they accept TTL 1–7 days, we can keep a compromise.

I’ll turn this into a short 2-pager and attach to the clause for legal review.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: technical-ephemeral-mode-onepager.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@medisync.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Medisync Legal <legal@medisync.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed exception language and next steps (Medisync / Redwood)

Hi Elena / Alan — following our thread and the SE notes, attached is proposed contract language we can include as an addendum to the SOW. Key points in the draft: 

- Data handling carveout (proposed): 
  * Redwood will enable Ephemeral Mode for the Medisync tenant in production, configured to:
    - Ensure raw audio and raw clinical transcripts containing PHI are not written to persistent logs or storage and are discarded immediately after processing.
    - Emit a purge event to the tenant audit log at the time of session teardown.
  * Derived artifacts (e.g., embeddings) used for personalization will be configured with a default TTL of 7 days; Medisync may request TTL=0 for specific datasets by written instruction and subject to feature impact.
  * If Medisync requires a legal guarantee of zero persistence for any derived artifact, Redwood will offer Dedicated deployment with customer-controlled KMS (pricing to be provided under a separate quote).

- Evidence & attestation: Redwood will provide a sanitized sample audit export showing purge events and a SOC2 control excerpt under NDA.

Next steps and timeline: 
- Medisync legal to review attached proposed-data-exception-clause.docx by 2026-11-24.
- Ben to share the ephemeral_mode one-pager and a sanitized sample purge log (target: 2026-11-22).
- Jonas to update HubSpot (deal MDX-8742) with chosen path (hosted-ephemeral vs dedicated) and confirm procurement timeline.

If this language broadly matches what you need, Alan — please confirm and we will circulate a redline-ready Word doc for your counsel. Happy to schedule a 20-min legal/SE alignment call if it helps.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Compliance & Privacy | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed-data-exception-clause.docx, medisync-privacy-ask-summary.pdf
